statement: Whenever count_subarrays returns a result r, r equals the number of pairs (i, j) of integers such that 0 <= i <= j < len(nums) and, for every k with i <= k < j, nums[k] < nums[k+1].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, count_subarrays returns a result r; it does not fail due to overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever count_subarrays returns a result r, r >= len(nums).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever count_subarrays returns a result r, r <= len(nums) * (len(nums) + 1) / 2, where the arithmetic is in mathematical integers.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever count_subarrays returns a result r, r = len(nums) * (len(nums) + 1) / 2 if and only if for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums) - 1, nums[i] < nums[i+1].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever count_subarrays returns a result r, r = len(nums) if and only if for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums) - 1, nums[i] >= nums[i+1].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever count_subarrays returns a result r, if the maximal strictly increasing runs of nums are the intervals [l_1, r_1], ..., [l_m, r_m] in increasing index order, where an interval [l, r] satisfies 0 <= l <= r < len(nums), nums[k] < nums[k+1] for every k with l <= k < r, and is maximal (l = 0 or nums[l-1] >= nums[l], and r = len(nums)-1 or nums[r] >= nums[r+1]), then r = sum_{t=1}^m ((r_t - l_t + 1) * (r_t - l_t + 2) / 2).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever count_subarrays returns a result r, for each i with 0 <= i < len(nums), let L_i be the largest integer m such that 1 <= m <= len(nums) - i and for every k with i <= k < i + m - 1, nums[k] < nums[k+1]. Then r = sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} L_i.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever count_subarrays returns a result r on nums, for every p with 1 <= p < len(nums) and nums[p-1] >= nums[p], if the function returns r_left on the prefix nums[0..p-1] and r_right on the suffix nums[p..len(nums)-1], then r = r_left + r_right.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: If for every i with 0 <= i < len(x) - 1, x[i] < x[i+1] if and only if y[i] < y[i+1], then whenever count_subarrays returns r_x on x and r_y on y, r_x = r_y.
preconditions: Both x and y satisfy 1 <= len(x) = len(y) <= 100000 and all elements of x and y are between 1 and 1000000.

statement: Whenever count_subarrays returns a result r, r >= len(nums) + (the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) - 1 and nums[i] < nums[i+1]).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.
